People kit

The one way people are drawn on this site. Faceless, slim, flat, in the site's own colours and shapes. The cast matches the names used in the example data, so the same person looks the same everywhere they appear.

The cast

You wear the brand teal; everyone else wears a muted colour of their own. Amber is never clothing, because amber means "still open".

Three scenes to build from

Pick the scene by the moment, not by variety. Each holds a with and a without version by swapping what's in hand (the prep card) and what's said.

A · Across the table

An in-person 1:1. The most human of the three; use for the headline moment in a section.

B · On a call

A remote or hybrid 1:1, which is most of the audience. Name tags carry the ownership dot (teal for you).

C · As a conversation

When the words matter more than the room: several lines of an exchange, avatars instead of bodies.

Rules

  • Sparingly: only where the moment is between people, chiefly the 1:1. A handful of scenes per page at most.
  • No faces. Hair, skin tone, glasses, a beard and clothing colour carry the person.
  • Slim proportions are fixed in cast.mjs (head r22, torso 64 wide). Scale the whole figure, never stretch it.
  • Speech is set in Newsreader, the page's voice for a person thinking or talking. Product things stay as white surfaces with pills and marks.
  • New people are added to the cast in cast.mjs with a name, so they stay consistent across pages. Keep the mix of genders, skin tones and hair.
